leads.title: Inter-American Court of Human Rights - Advisory Opinion of 9 January 2018
leads.documents: Holds parties to the American Convention on Human Rights should grant same-sex couples access to all family registration including marriage, and that recognition of gender identity on official documents is a human right protected by the Convention; article states Guatemala is legally bound by it
leads.detail: Cited as '9 January 2018' IACHR advisory opinion on American Convention on Human Rights; no URL visible in text

leads.title: Initiative 5272 - Protection of Life and Family Act / Ley de Proteccion a la Vida y la Familia
leads.documents: Congressional bill to explicitly ban same-sex marriage, define family as 'a father, a mother and children', increase penalties for abortion/criminalize miscarriage, protect refusal to accept non-heterosexual conduct as normal, describes homosexuality as 'contrary to biology and genetics'; passed first and second readings, third reading blocked Sept 2018
leads.detail: Cited as Initiative 5272; statements by President Jimmy Morales invoking Article 156; no URL visible

leads.title: Law 5272 vote of 9 March 2022 - archived 15 March 2022
leads.documents: 2022 failed attempt to ban same-sex marriage and penalize abortion with 5 years prison; approved by Congress March 9, veto threatened by President Alejandro Giammattei as violating Constitution and international agreements, archived/discarded March 15
leads.detail: Cited with dates March 9, 2022 approval and March 15 archiving; no URL visible

leads.title: Codigo de la Ninez y la Juventud (Code on Childhood and Youth) 1997 - repealed 2003
leads.documents: Sole non-discrimination exception cited: safeguarded children and youth from discrimination based on various factors including their sexual orientation and that of their parents; later repealed in 2003 leaving no SOGI protection in employment, education, housing, health, banking, public accommodations
leads.detail: Cited as approved 1997, repealed 2003; no URL visible

leads.title: Criminal Code reform bill May 2017 - Articles 27 and 202
leads.documents: Proposal by Deputy Sandra Moran to add sexual orientation and gender identity as protected categories in Criminal Code provisions on aggravating circumstances / discrimination
leads.detail: Cited as presented May 2017 by Deputy Sandra Moran to Congress; no URL visible

leads.title: Gender identity bill introduced December 2017 - rejected August 2018
leads.documents: Bill to recognize right to gender identity and allow transgender people to change name and gender on birth certificates; documents current rule since 2016 allowing legal name change with judicial permission but no legal gender change
leads.detail: Cited as introduced Dec 2017, rejected Aug 2018 by Legislative and Constitutional Points Commission and Women's Commission; no URL visible

leads.title: Bill 5490 advanced December 2021
leads.documents: Bill to remove education regarding transgender individuals in schools to protect children from 'gender identity disorders' and require censorship of media with transgender individuals; unanimously approved by Congress Education, Science and Technology Commission for full congress review
leads.detail: Cited as Bill 5490 Dec 2021 with AllOutAction petition 17,250 signatures as of Nov 2024; no URL visible

leads.title: Human Rights Watch - 2023 report on Guatemala
leads.documents: Reports individuals cannot self-report gender for official documents - must use sex/name assigned at birth - blocking education and basic services requiring official ID; reports active conversion therapy centers funded by Evangelical churches in rural areas with electroshock, corrective rape, forced marriage/coerced sex; corrective rape not recognized as hate crime only as rape
leads.detail: Cited as 'From the 2023 Human Rights Watch'; no URL visible in text

leads.title: United Nations and NGO reports late 1990s on 'social cleansing campaign'
leads.documents: Reports that LGBT people in Guatemala were systematically targeted for death; bias-motivated crimes on sexual orientation/gender identity reportedly tolerated by Government especially against transgender people; example victim transgender AIDS activist Luis Palencia gunned down Guatemala City 1997
leads.detail: Cited as late-1990s UN and NGO reports; victim Luis Palencia 1997; no URL visible

leads.title: Political Constitution of the Republic of Guatemala - Article 156
leads.documents: Constitutional provision invoked by President Jimmy Morales to claim institutions/officials 'are not obligated to follow illegal orders' in refusing IACHR same-sex marriage/gender identity ruling; article notes usage of 'illegal' is factually incorrect given oath to uphold international law and IACHR jurisdiction
leads.detail: Cited as Article 156 Political Constitution quote from Morales: 'Guatemala believe in the family based in the marriage of man and woman'; no URL visible
